rows.observations: 10. The reliability and completeness of the PPE - Medical Equipment account balance totaling P1.825 billion could not be ascertained due to the following: a. Discrepancies between the OCAT SLs and the CGSO RPCPPE amounting to P1.181 billion, due to: • PPE items recorded in the OCAT but not in RPCPPE amounting to P0.776 billion; • PPE items that were recorded in the RPCPPE but not in the OCAT, totaling P2.017 billion; • PPE items amounting to P0.061 billion that could not be reconciled due to insufficient data or description on both records; and b. PPE items amounting to P0.174 billion were incorrectly classified under the Medical Equipment account.
rows.recommendations: 10.11. We recommended that Management direct: a.The OCAT to: • Coordinate with the CGSO to addres inconsistencies in the PPE items and properly account for them in the accounting records; • Prepare the necessary information required b COA Circular No. 2020-006, and conduct the procedures provided therein for the implementation of the one-time cleansing of PPE in the books; and • Prepare adjusting entries to correct th misclassified Medical Equipment items.
rows.action_plan: based on RPCPPE report of 2024 and inventory results of the one-time cleansing, based and guided by COA Circular 2020-006

rows.observations: These are not in accordance with Paragraph 27 of the IPSAS 1, and Section 6.3 of COA Circular No. 2020-006. These discrepancies between the OCAT and CGSO records adversely affected the accuracy and validity of the reported balances of PPE-Medical Equipment
rows.recommendations: b.The CGSO to: • Coordinate with the OCAT for the reconciliatio of PPE records against the RPCPPE, and address issues pertaining to PPEs found at stations during the physical count; and • Prepare the requirements per COA Circular No. 2020-006 and expedite the procedures outlined therein for the one-time cleansing of PPE.
